text:
The Devils are the best team in the East by the chances and they are acting like it: five straight wins, 9-1-0 in their last ten, and 59% of the expected goals this season. That isn't a hot streak riding on bounces. Their finishing is right where their chances say it should be, and their goaltending has been slightly worse than expected, which is a strange thing to say about a team that traded for Connor Hellebuyck on Oct. 23.

Hellebuyck is the story this week. He got his first shutout as a Devil in Toronto on Sunday, and New Jersey then said he won't start in Winnipeg on Tuesday, the city he left after requesting a trade. "This is a goaltender that's not going to play every night... it just made sense," Sheldon Keefe said, per Daily Faceoff. Expect that to be the loudest building of his month.

The engine is up front and on the back end. Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Arseny Gritsyuk have outscored teams 11-3 with 65% of the chances, and Nico Hischier's line with Timo Meier and Luke Evangelista isn't far behind. Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes are 19-9 in goals together. They also take only 2.6 penalties a game while drawing 3.9. Our simulations make them a 95% playoff team projecting around 107 points. The only thing to watch is health, and that week in Winnipeg.
